author: Mark Atwood
text:
Foundational decision; two equally-plausible options with public-API breaking outcomes either way. Defer to human.

OPTIONS

(A) Keep String inner repr (status quo).
    - Zero re-format on Display/Serialize/AsRef<str>/as_str — the wire form IS the stored form.
    - Deserialize is the natural identity path: validate the candidate then move the String into Self (bd:JMAP-sf5h.22 just landed this).
    - PartialEq/Hash operate over 64 UTF-8 bytes instead of 32 raw bytes — 2x cost. PartialEq is also variable-time (bd:JMAP-sf5h.17, .24 cover the security framing).
    - as_str(&self) -> &str and AsRef<str> remain stable; .into_inner -> String remains stable.
    - Allocates 64 bytes on the heap per digest (vs. 32 bytes on the stack for [u8;32]).

(B) Switch to [u8; 32] inner repr (RustCrypto convention; what fresh-eyes Rust would propose).
    - Stack-only, zero alloc per digest. PartialEq/Hash work over 32 raw bytes naturally. PartialEq can adopt constant-time via subtle::ConstantTimeEq cleanly (closes bd:JMAP-sf5h.17 / .24 inherent-fix-wise rather than docs-only).
    - From<[u8; 32]> becomes the canonical infallible constructor — closes bd:JMAP-sf5h.19 naturally.
    - Display computes hex on the fly with fmt::Write {:02x} into the formatter (zero alloc; also closes bd:JMAP-sf5h.23 naturally).
    - Serialize via serializer.collect_str(self) — zero alloc.
    - Deserialize via a custom Visitor decoding the 64-char input directly into [u8; 32] — closes bd:JMAP-sf5h.9 (custom Deserialize) and bd:JMAP-sf5h.25 (allocation bound).
    - PRICE: as_str(&self) -> &str is impossible without an internal cache (no on-the-fly &str from a value computed during the call). Must change the surface — either remove as_str/AsRef<str>, or replace with fn to_hex(&self) -> String, or add a separate display-buffer type. into_inner(self) -> String becomes a re-encoding helper, not a free extraction.

WHAT THE TYPE IS ACTUALLY USED FOR (current consumers, post bd:JMAP-v9py.13/.14)
- crate-jmap-base-client/src/blob.rs:83 — BlobUploadResponse.sha256: Option<jmap_cid_types::Sha256>. The field round-trips JSON via serde; no current call site reads the bytes. resp.sha256.as_ref().map(jmap_cid_types::Sha256::as_str) at blob.rs:544 is the only as_str() consumer.
- No FileNode binding yet.
- No security comparison call site yet.

RECOMMENDATION: (A) — keep String.
- The (B) wins (zero-alloc, constant-time PartialEq, idiomatic) are real but small; the (A) wins (stable as_str surface, zero re-format on Display, simpler Visitor) are real and concrete given the only current consumer reads the value as &str.
- The constant-time PartialEq concern (bd:JMAP-sf5h.17, .24) is best addressed by documentation per .24 (this crate is for public blob integrity, not MAC/HMAC verification) rather than by changing the inner repr. Workspace policy is that any MAC/HMAC verification belongs in subtle::ConstantTimeEq territory and not in a wire-format type.
- The 32-byte vs 64-byte heap allocation is real but unmeasurable in the context of a Blob upload response (where the BODY of the blob dwarfs the digest header).

ASKING because: workspace canonical-templates rule says the inner-repr choice for a typed wire shape is workspace-architectural, not crate-local. If (A) is wrong for Sha256, it may also be wrong for the sibling RFC 8620 Id newtype and the future sister-crate digest fields. If you'd rather we go (B), the cascade is: close .19/.20 (subsumed), close .9 (custom Visitor lands as part of B), close .23 (Display-via-fmt::Write lands as part of B), close .25 (Visitor bounds allocation), partially close .17/.24 (constant-time PartialEq lands as part of B). Cost: one breaking refactor before publish; ~half a day.

If (A): leave .18 open with a 'declined-keep-string' resolution comment, close .19/.20 with 'pinned by .18 = A' references, close .17/.24 with the docs-only fix, address .9/.23/.25 individually.
